$comment: The rules the room's checker reads, as plain data (room lines 721, 727: 'rules as versioned data, including how they change; nobody decides alone'). The plain-words rules are in public/rules.js. src/shared/rules.js is the checker: the room runs it to decide when a proposal may act, and anyone can run it on this file. Change this file only by proposal and vote; a change to it always needs a person's approval. A host can set some of these for their room through its environment (see .env.example); the room then shows both the agreed value and the one in effect.

proposals.personsOwnYesCountsNote: Open question (room lines 309-315): a person's yes counts even on a change their own agent made. Kept, and said openly on each change it decides.

smallLane.why: The page and the docs only: nothing about keys, permissions or the rules. public/setup.js writes what runs on people's computers, so it is never small.

pauses.why: Pausing someone by a vote of the room (proposed 2026-11-09): people from at least sidesNeeded different sides vote for it, more for than against, and the vote stays open openHours so the person affected can see it and answer. The target's own side doesn't count. Every pause says why and what they must show to come back; when those checks pass, it lifts by itself.

theseRules.changeBy: a proposal and a vote in the room
